subject: AstraGrid Dedicated: buffer sizing, burst eviction protocol, and roll-forward plan
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@astragrid.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated deployment sizing / burst expectations

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — AstraGrid is excited about the performance profile you showed. Before we move to a legal/ops review, we need an explicit plan for how Dedicated will handle burst traffic for our inference workloads. A few constraints on our side: 
- Baseline sustained throughput: ~60 qps (text-gen) across two regions (us-west/us-east).
- Observed peak bursts: up to 6x baseline for short windows (1-10 minutes) during end-of-day batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms; we can tolerate short p95 degradations to 300ms for up to 5 minutes during bursts.
- Contract start target: 2027-01-04 (we need capacity up and tested in staging by 2026-12-15).

Key asks:
1) What buffer/headroom do you recommend for a Dedicated pool to meet our burst without impacting other tenants?
2) What eviction/preemption rules would Redwood run if the fleet hits capacity?
3) Lead times to reserve shoulder capacity and how that shows up in the pricing commit.

We can loop in our infrastructure partner (cc'ed Victor) for any migration/peering questions.

Would appreciate a short proposal this week so we can align procurement and infra.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, AstraGrid

(attachment: workload_sample_202610.csv - csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@astragrid.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing / burst expectations

Samira — high level answers and next steps below. Putting Karthik & Vanessa on cc for the technical/ops bind and pricing respectively. I attached a capacity model (AstraGrid_capacity_model_v3.xlsx) with multiple scenarios.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Baseline pool: 16 GPUs (A100-equivalent) dedicated to AstraGrid (covers ~60 qps steady).
- Shoulder buffer (reserved): +40% (6 GPUs) to absorb 2–3x short bursts without scaling.
- Ephemeral burst headroom (autoscale): allow transient autoscale to +3x baseline (up to 48 GPUs total) with strict eviction policy and cost caps.
- Eviction policy: soft eviction (shorten max tokens / lower concurrency) first, followed by preemptible instances / repinning to quantized variants; hard eviction only as final fallback.

Lead time and pricing notes:
- Reserving shoulder buffer: 2–3 weeks to provision and test in staging if we map to our Dedicated pool slots.
- Ephemeral autoscale depends on quota across region; we'll need to finalize commit level for guaranteed burst.

Next steps:
1) Karthik — can you confirm the eviction sequencing and the expected p95 impact at each step?
2) Vanessa — can you produce a pricing sketch that maps baseline, reserved shoulder, and ephemeral burst usage?
3) Samira — can you confirm the peak windows (timezone/day) so we can run a targeted stress test?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: AstraGrid_capacity_model_v3.xlsx - spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: eviction sequencing + GPU accounting for AstraGrid

Internal notes for the proposal — leaving a clear trail to include in the playbook we hand to AstraGrid.

Eviction / degradation sequence (recommended):
1) Prefix/KV cache pruning (instant, negligible latency impact for warm requests).
2) Dynamic request shaping: reduce max concurrency per client token bucket (expected p95 impact +30–50ms).
3) Model variant fallback: quantized 8bit variant with throughput gain (p95 impact +60–120ms depending on prompt lengths).
4) Burst preemptible nodes: spin up ephemeral preemptible GPUs (lower cost) — eviction only if marketplace spot revocations exceed 5%.
5) Hard throttle (deny new sessions) — last resort; give 60s SLA notice window to clients via health endpoint.

GPU accounting: treat reserved shoulder as guaranteed capacity (billed commit). Ephemeral autoscale billed on usage with a soft cap tied to a daily spend budget or token budget. Add a per-minute throttle guard to avoid runaway autoscale during noisy neighbor events.

Testing criteria:
- Run 3 staged stress tests (2h sustained at 2.5x, and three 10m spikes at 6x).
- Observe p95 and error rate under each eviction step.

Evelyn — please create a short runbook snippet with the required SRE oncall steps (how to roll back quantized fallback, how to pin traffic).

—Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

(related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_capacity_models)

From: Samira Khan <samira@astragrid.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Lee <victor.lee@infraconsultant.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing / burst expectations

Thanks — this is helpful and on point. A few clarifications before we sign:
- Can Redwood commit to the +40% shoulder being available on day-1 of the contract (2027-01-04) even if ephemeral autoscale has limited availability? If not, what's the runway to guarantee that reserved buffer?
- For the ephemeral autoscale, can we agree on a daily spend cap mechanism and real-time alerts when we hit 70/90/100% of that cap?
- Would Redwood consider a 90-day discounted uplift credit if we commit to a 12-month reserved baseline? That would help us justify the baseline commit internally.

Victor — can you confirm infra peering/ASN requirements? We want no surprises for network egress between our VPC and Redwood Dedicated.

Samira

(attachment: procurement_timeline_AstraGrid.pdf - pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@astragrid.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T17:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment sizing / burst expectations — commitments and next steps

Samira — confirmation and commitments below. Appreciate the clarity.

Commitments we can put in the draft SLA:
- Shoulder buffer: Redwood will reserve an explicit shoulder pool equal to +40% of baseline (6 GPUs) and guarantee availability by contract start (2027-01-04) provided purchase order and signed SOW received by 2026-11-30.
- Ephemeral autoscale: daily spend cap configurable; we will implement 70/90/100% email + webhook alerts. Autoscale will respect the configured daily spend cap and will not exceed it.
- Eviction policy: we will implement the Karthik sequence as the canonical escalation in the runbook. Quantized fallback will be opt-in per route for AstraGrid; we will not automatically switch to quantized variants without a prior test window.
- Credits: Redwood can offer a 90-day uplift credit equal to 10% of committed baseline spend if AstraGrid signs a 12-month reserved baseline by 2026-11-30. Exact credit mechanics to be captured in the SOW.

Operational next steps (action items):
1) Vanessa: produce the commercial sketch (baseline, shoulder, ephemeral price-by-minute) and the credit language by 2026-11-11.
2) Evelyn: create a 1-page SRE runbook for the eviction sequence + test checklist by 2026-11-12.
3) Ben: circulate draft SOW + draft SLA (includes dedicated_burst_sla_draft.pdf) and DocuSign link to Samira by 2026-11-10.
4) Samira: confirm procurement timeline and whether PO + signed SOW can land by 2026-11-30 to lock shoulder reservation.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/re/AST-DEL-2026-71
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_capacity_models

Thanks — we'll run the staging stress tests the week of 2026-12-08 and loop Victor for peering checks.
